Before measurement, observe the symbol markings on the dial to understand the instrument's performance characteristics, and carefully read the instrument's operating instructions to understand the precautions for use and the required working conditions (mounting position, temperature, external magnetic field, AC current waveform and frequency).

During measurement, connect the instrument correctly to the circuit under test. For example, when using a voltmeter to measure the voltage between two points in a circuit, connect the two test probes directly across these two points; when using an ammeter to measure the current in the branch containing a certain point in a circuit, first disconnect the conductor at that point, then connect the two broken ends to the two test probes of the ammeter respectively.
For instruments requiring mechanical or electrical zero adjustment, set the indication to zero before measurement. For pointer-type instruments, keep the eye directly facing the pointer when reading.

Voltmeters, ammeters and wattmeters used on ships shall have clear markings on their dials indicating their rated values. The instrument casing must not be opened arbitrarily, nor the internal mechanism removed.

It is strictly forbidden to place instruments beside generators, motors or heavy-current conductors, or in locations with high temperature, rapid hot-cold changes, corrosive gases, or damp and dark conditions.

Before using a multimeter to measure a quantity, the position of the selector switch and the jack in which the test leads are inserted must match the quantity to be measured, and check whether the pointer is at zero; otherwise, perform zero adjustment.
During measurement with a multimeter, the position of the selector switch must not be changed arbitrarily.

When measuring resistance in a circuit, at least one end of the resistor under test must be completely disconnected from the circuit, and the power supply in the circuit must be switched off. If capacitors exist in the circuit, discharge them before measurement; never measure resistance with the circuit energized. Before measurement, perform electrical zero adjustment, and re-adjust zero each time the range is changed.

Before measuring voltage or current, if the pointer is not at zero, perform mechanical zero adjustment first. When measuring voltage or current, if the upper limit of the range of the voltage or current to be measured cannot be determined, set the selector switch to the maximum range, then adjust the selector switch to a suitable range according to the actual measurement conditions while disconnected from the measurement point.
When measuring 2500V AC or DC voltage, insert the red test lead into the "2500V" jack and pay attention to safety.

When measuring DC voltage or current, observe the polarity of the instrument. When measuring voltage, connect the red test lead to the point of higher potential in the circuit under test; when measuring current, the current shall flow into the meter through the red test lead.
A multimeter is only suitable for measuring the effective value of sinusoidal voltage or current, and cannot measure non-sinusoidal quantities.
After using a multimeter, set the selector switch to the maximum AC voltage range to ensure instrument safety.

Since the current through the meter measuring mechanism is fixed and a magnetoelectric measuring mechanism can only pass microampere-level current, different conversion circuits are required to measure various electrical quantities and ranges.
The multimeter has a complex structure and many types, with differing layouts of selector switches and jacks; read the instruction manual carefully before use.
